label: AQA-style practice (Revision-authored, not an AQA question)

question.context: Northside Cycles is reviewing its monthly budget for replacement parts used in repairs.
question.stem:
In April, Northside Cycles budgeted £18,500 for replacement parts. Actual spending on replacement parts was £21,200.

Calculate the replacement-parts cost variance using actual cost − budgeted cost. State whether the variance is favourable or adverse for profit.

points.descriptor: Calculates the variance by subtracting budgeted cost from actual cost.
Correctly identifies the cost variance as adverse for profit because actual spending exceeded the budget.
accept: adverse because costs were £2,700 above budget

mark_scheme.model_answer:
Variance = actual cost − budgeted cost
= £21,200 − £18,500
= £2,700 adverse

It is adverse for profit because replacement-parts spending was above budget.
